def: The stored keys and values of all earlier tokens at every layer, kept so that each new token's attention does not recompute them.
The first phase of generation, in which the whole prompt is processed in parallel and its keys and values are written to the cache.
The phase of generation that produces one token per step, reading all the weights and the whole cache each time.
The delay between sending a request and receiving the first generated token, set mainly by prefill and so by the prompt length.
The time between successive generated tokens, set by the cost of one decode step.
The number of floating-point operations a job performs per byte it moves from memory, which decides whether compute or bandwidth limits it.
A plot in which attainable speed is the smaller of the compute peak and memory bandwidth times arithmetic intensity, with a ridge point where the two meet.
Limited by how fast data can be read from memory rather than by arithmetic speed, as single-stream decoding is.
Attention in which all query heads share a single key-value head, shrinking the KV cache by the number of heads.
Attention in which groups of query heads share a key-value head, an intermediate between multi-head and multi-query attention that cuts the cache by the group size.
The cache cost of one token: 2 times layers times key-value heads times head width times bytes per number.
